units.function: Pure unit tests for selecting an Issue goal from an explicit value, a linked Project's goal or the Company default during create and update.
units.dependencyDirection: Current and requested Project/Goal IDs plus Project and Company fallback IDs enter pure resolver functions; one nullable Goal ID is returned to the Issue service.
units.keyDataModels: Current/requested Project ID, current/requested Goal ID, Project Goal ID, Company default Goal ID and nullable resolved Goal ID.
units.lifecycle: Creation prefers explicit Goal, then Project Goal for a linked Project, otherwise Company default; updates backfill legacy nulls, replace inferred fallback values after Project changes and preserve values judged explicit.
units.testAssessment: Eight concise cases cover the intended precedence and common legacy/project transitions. Missing are an explicit assignment-origin field, the ambiguous case where a user explicitly chose the same ID as a fallback, intentional clearing, default-Goal changes, deleted/archived or cross-Company Goals, multi-Goal Projects, concurrent changes and provenance of automatic reassignment.
units.designRationale: Keep ordinary Issues connected to a useful organizational Goal and migrate old unassigned records without requiring a bulk data rewrite.
units.companyOsProblem: A Work item must retain whether its Goal was explicitly chosen by a human, inherited from a Project/template or supplied by organization policy because that origin affects accountability and later recomputation.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE_ONLY for the precedence scenarios. Company OS tests must operate on a persisted GoalAssignment value containing origin, policy/template version and actor, and must prove explicit choices are never reclassified merely because their ID equals a current fallback.
units.responsibilityConflict: ID equality is used to infer human intent. An explicit selection equal to the fallback can be silently rewritten after a Project change, and an automatic backfill has no actor/policy evidence in the returned value.

units.function: Pure create/update resolver that stores only the selected Goal ID and heuristically distinguishes explicit assignments from inherited fallback assignments.
units.dependencyDirection: Issue service supplies current/requested identifiers and already-resolved Project/Company fallbacks; the helper has no database or authorization dependency and returns a nullable string.
units.keyDataModels: MaybeId inputs and one Goal ID without assignment-origin, actor, policy version or effective time.
units.lifecycle: Create applies explicit/Project/Company precedence; update computes current and next fallback, substitutes next fallback for missing or fallback-equal current values and otherwise keeps the current Goal.
units.testAssessment: The implementation is readable and deterministic, but its representation cannot distinguish explicit-equal-to-fallback from inherited state. Passing goalId:null requests fallback rather than a durable explicit-none state, and the helper cannot validate tenant ownership, Goal lifecycle or policy version.
units.designRationale: Achieve automatic Goal inheritance and legacy backfill with a small stateless helper and no schema migration for assignment metadata.
units.companyOsProblem: Responsibility chains require goal assignment intent and provenance to survive policy, Project and organization-template changes.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT with a GoalAssignment aggregate/value object: goalId or explicit-none, origin enum, source Project/template/policy version, assignedBy Principal, assignedAt and replacement reason. Recalculation becomes an explicit command/event rather than an ID-equality heuristic.
units.responsibilityConflict: The algorithm can overwrite a human's explicit intent and cannot answer who assigned the Goal or why it changed. This directly conflicts with Company OS's accountable-human and responsibility-record requirements.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres migration/service integration tests proving a Project icon and explicit color round-trip while omitted icon/color values remain null.
units.dependencyDirection: Company seed data and Project create input enter projectService; all database migrations run in an embedded Postgres instance and getById reads the stored presentation fields.
units.keyDataModels: Company, Project name, nullable icon identifier, nullable color string and migration 0094 schema state.
units.lifecycle: Create with icon or color persists and reads it; omission leaves each field null so the UI applies a neutral presentation rather than a server-assigned color.
units.testAssessment: A real migrated database gives useful schema/service round-trip evidence and covers null defaults. It does not test update/clear/import/export, Company-scoped reads, API enum rejection, arbitrary database values, unknown icon fallback, color format, concurrent updates or compatibility when the design-system catalog changes.
units.designRationale: Persist user-selected visual identity while keeping new Projects neutral until an explicit presentation choice is made.
units.companyOsProblem: Warm Chinese Web and future office projections need stable semantic presentation references without coupling Core to a specific icon/component catalog.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE_ONLY the migrated-database round-trip and nullable neutral default. Store a versioned semantic appearance token in a Web/Projection-owned model, validate at the API boundary and define graceful fallback; do not put Raft assets, icon enums or renderer types in Core/Application.
units.responsibilityConflict: Icon/color are presentation metadata and must not imply Project status, risk, ownership or approval. Direct service use bypasses the API enum validator, showing why display metadata cannot carry authority semantics.
